articles.title: How bug bounty sharpens one researcher’s security skills
articles.summary:
As Cybersecurity Awareness Month continues, the GitHub Bug Bounty team is excited to spotlight another top-performing security researcher from the GitHub Security Bug Bounty Program: @r31n!
As home to the world’s developers, GitHub is dedicated to the security and reliability of the code behind millions of projects, and our Bug Bounty Program remains a cornerstone of that commitment. Collaboration with external researchers is one of the most effective ways to improve security, and every year, the community helps us identify and fix vulnerabilities that make the platform safer for everyone.
The security research landscape is changing rapidly. AI has lowered the barrier to entry and become a genuine force multiplier. We use it across our own internal security programs, and we welcome researchers who do the same. However, what separates great research has not changed: validation, a working proof of concept, and a clear demonstration of real security impact. The tools do not matter; the quality of the work does. The researchers we spotlight this month exemplify exactly that standard through findings that are verified, reproducible, and demonstrate that a security boundary has been crossed rather than simply theorizing that one exists.

Anthropic said the new agent is meant to cater to professionals and small businesses to help them with automating and managing tasks. The company is making a distinction from personal agents such as Instinct, by noting that Duet isn’t good at handling errands or booking tickets, and it can’t show you its browser use as it happens.
Instead, Duet can build a daily briefing for its users, create dashboards, or suggest actions based on the user’s data. Like other agents, Duet can complete tasks in the background through its own virtual machine while you handle other things, then come back to you if it needs your approval.
The launch arrives as the market shifts beyond AI assistants to agents that can work on users’ behalf. Many of Anthropic’s rivals are focusing on business use cases. While Meta’s Muse is a personal AI assistant, the company also released a version to cater to small businesses with connections to other apps. OpenAI’s Dots has a business slant as well, with its integration with professional tools.

articles.title: EUA ampliam vigilância após detectar mosca-da-bicheira em animal selvagem
articles.summary:
O parasita conhecido como mosca-da-bicheira do Novo Mundo foi detectado pela primeira vez em décadas em um animal silvestre nos Estados Unidos. O Departamento de Agricultura do país (USDA, na sigla em inglês) confirmou nesta quarta-feira (21) a presença do organismo em uma fêmea de alce encontrada no condado de Pecos, no Texas.
O animal estava em propriedade destinada à caça e o caso foi identificado depois que um caçador abateu o alce. Uma amostra foi encaminhada a um laboratório especializado em insetos que afetam a pecuária, em Kerrville, também no Texas, onde a presença do parasita foi confirmada.
A descoberta levou as autoridades a ampliar a vigilância de animais silvestres na região. A Comissão de Saúde Animal do Texas também vai modificar uma zona de infestação estabelecida anteriormente.
O episódio ocorre em meio ao avanço da mosca-da-bicheira pela América do Norte e aumenta a preocupação com a disseminação do parasita entre animais silvestres e rebanhos.
Segundo caso é confirmado em outro estado

articles.title: Un estudio propone usar agua salada y contaminada para refrigerar los centros de datos que alimentan la IA
articles.summary:
Los centros de datos que sostienen la inteligencia artificial, la nube y el procesamiento en tiempo real consumen cantidades enormes de energía. Toda esa electricidad se convierte en calor residual que debe eliminarse para evitar que los equipos se sobrecalienten, y el método más extendido para lograrlo recurre a un insumo cada vez más escaso: agua dulce. Solo en Estados Unidos, la demanda hídrica de estas instalaciones podría multiplicarse hasta cuatro veces hacia 2028, hasta alcanzar entre 150.000 y 270.000 millones de litros anuales, según las estimaciones recogidas en el estudio.
La presión sobre los recursos locales ya disparó alarmas regulatorias. Por ejemplo, en septiembre, el gobernador de Texas, Greg Abbott, ordenó una pausa en los permisos para nuevos centros de datos, y la fiscalía general del estado abrió una investigación sobre el consumo hídrico de las instalaciones existentes.
Frente a ese panorama, un grupo de ingenieros y geocientíficos planteó una pregunta directa: ¿puede el agua salada o contaminada, que hoy se descarta como residuo industrial, servir para refrigerar esas instalaciones y aliviar así la competencia por el agua potable? La respuesta, según sus hallazgos, es que la tecnología necesaria ya existe y que incluso las opciones más demandantes en energía representan apenas una fracción menor del consumo eléctrico total de un centro de datos.

articles.title: Localizing compliance at scale: Achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification
articles.summary:
Localizing compliance at scale: achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification
For ten days, auditors appointed by the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA) sat together with us and worked through 80 controls. That is what it took for a company headquartered in the United States, operating a global network serving Korean users, to be certified in South Korea. Cloudflare has now obtained South Korea's Information Security Management System (ISMS) certification under the ISMS-P framework.
For customers in Korea, this is more than a compliance checkbox. It is evidence that Cloudflare's security and privacy program has been examined not only for whether our controls exist, but for how they operate in the context of Korean law, the Korean language, and the particular expectations of Korean regulators.
What a Korean user sees when they sign up
The most visible result of this work is the Cloudflare account sign-up page. In most parts of the world, the line that sits above the sign-up button reads: "By continuing, I agree to Cloudflare's terms, privacy policy, and cookie policy."
A user signing up from South Korea sees something different. The Korean experience is triggered by the country selected at sign-up and by IP geolocation from within South Korea, and it breaks the same agreement into four separately labeled items, each marked required or optional, each linking to its full text, with an option to agree to all of them at once:
- 모두 동의 (Agree to all)

articles.summary:
AI developers aren’t just running a single model anymore—they’re orchestrating multiple models in parallel, chaining inference calls, and experimenting with frontier-class architectures that demand hundreds of gigabytes of memory. NVIDIA DGX Spark was built to bring AI development to the desk, and now you’ll be able to link even more Spark nodes together.
At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA announced official support for eight-node DGX Spark clusters, scaling unified memory to 1 TB and opening the door to frontier-class models, multi-agent workloads, and near-linear pre-training—all running locally.
NVIDIA Sync makes it easy to cluster. Its Cluster Assistant handles setup and device management. Support for eight-node clusters in NVIDIA Sync is coming by the end of the year.
Read on for benchmark data on how inference, orchestration, and training scale as the cluster grows.
Run larger, newer frontier-class models
The biggest benefit of an eight-node cluster is memory. A single DGX Spark provides 128 GB of unified memory; four nodes reach 512 GB; eight nodes reach 1 TB. That capacity opens the door to a class of models that previously wouldn’t start on a four-node system, including the full GLM 5.3 (753B) model from Z.ai.

articles.title: Developer platform Railway urges 'all users' to revoke secret keys after cyberattack | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Development platform Railway has confirmed that a cyberattack allowed hackers to access some customer secrets, prompting the company to urge all users to rotate their API and cloud keys amid fears of a broader breach of customer data.
The company, which allows customers to build apps and services on its cloud development platform, said in a blog post on Wednesday that the unidentified hackers “may have accessed encrypted environment variables and, for some of them, obtained the decrypted contents.”
These environment variables are typically lists of passwords and API keys that are used by the developer’s apps to access other services, such as cloud data storage and databases. With these customer secrets, an attacker could also log in and access data as if they were the rightful owner.
Railway said that while its initial analysis suggests the breach was limited to a “subset of users,” it suggested that “all users” should revoke and rotate all of their keys so that attackers cannot abuse them.
The company also said it briefly paused new builds and deployments while the company investigated, and began restoration soon after.
Railway did not say how many specific users were affected, or what was identified as the root cause. The company did not answer questions about the incident, or whether it has received any correspondence from hackers, such as a ransom demand. articles.summary:
C’est l’une des alertes de sécurité les plus sérieuses de ces dernières années. Depuis le mardi 20 octobre 2026, le monde de l’informatique est passé en alerte rouge à cause de PHP2Shell, un duo de failles débusquées dans le cœur de PHP. Pour ceux qui ne connaissent pas, PHP est un langage de programmation omniprésent sur Internet. Il fait tourner les coulisses d’une bonne partie du web, des petits blogs aux boutiques en ligne, en passant par d’importants systèmes de gestion de contenu comme WordPress, Drupal, Joomla ou Magento. Des centaines de millions de sites web reposent en fait sur PHP.
Les deux failles sont jugées « critiques » par les experts en cybersécurité. Pour éviter une explosion des cyberattaques, l’équipe de PHP n’a pas tardé à mettre en ligne des correctifs de toute urgence. Les versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 et 8.2.35 de PHP corrigent le tir et empêchent les pirates d’exploiter les vulnérabilités.

articles.title: Why Engineers Should Brave Capitol Hill
articles.summary:
When San Antonio–based software engineer Nikhil Jathar first went to Washington, D.C., to advocate for federal support for technology education and research funding, he was in awe of the opportunity. It was spring of 2025, not long after Jathar settled in the United States from India, when he got an invitation to join the annual Congressional Visits Day organized by IEEE-USA.
“My first reaction was, ‘Wow, I get to visit Congress,’ ” says Jathar, CTO of AvanSaber, a business software company he cofounded in 2014. At the time, he did not have a specific lobbying position on behalf of the company. But he was intrigued by the invitation—which goes out to all U.S. IEEE members—and as he read more about congressional visits, his motivation deepened. He realized: “I need to try this. I want to see where it goes.”
What’s Your Ask?
Congressional staffers expect clarity from advocates. Be clear on what you plan to ask for when you arrive. Here are some common options:
- Cosponsor (or oppose) an existing bill or amendment.
- Preserve, remove, or modify legislative text in a bill under consideration.
- Add language to an appropriations bill or committee report.
- Ask a federal agency a specific oversight question.
- Request a briefing, hearing, Government Accountability Office review, or stakeholder roundtable.
- Encourage an agency to clarify a technical rule.

articles.title: How to Read Data into GPU Memory in Python with NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
GPU applications are processing ever-growing datasets with increasingly powerful accelerators. According to the 2025 Stanford AI Index, compute for notable AI models has been doubling approximately every five months, while the size of datasets used to train LLMs has been doubling approximately every eight months. As computation and data scale together, moving data efficiently from storage becomes a necessity for keeping accelerators supplied.
NVIDIA Magnum IO GPUDirect Storage (GDS) addresses this challenge by enabling a direct data path between supported storage and GPU memory. This avoids unnecessary staging through CPU memory and reduces overall CPU utilization in the system. GDS is supported by a growing ecosystem that includes many major storage vendors.
At the application layer, Python plays a central role in modern AI development. As of August 2025, nearly half of all new AI projects on GitHub were built primarily in Python while the main application interface to GDS is the cuFile C API.
NVIDIA KvikIO, a Python and C++ library for high-performance file I/O, bridges this gap. It provides high-level, idiomatic Python and C++ interfaces, along with additional controls over how I/O requests are performed.
The tutorial in this post demonstrates how to use the NVIDIA KvikIO Python API to configure storage I/O, read data into GPU memory, and confirm that the accelerated path within GDS was activated. It also shows how to inspect the KvikIO and cuFile settings that influence t…

articles.title: Spotify's current AI bet is about being the music service that agents choose | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Spotify had a strong third quarter, reaching 788 million monthly active users and generating nearly €5 billion (around $5.6 billion USD) in revenue. But the more interesting takeaway from its earnings call was how the company sees people listening to music in the future, and why the rise of AI agents could be good news for its business.
Co-CEO Gustav Söderström thinks the music streaming giant is particularly well-suited to this shift.
“Spotify is in one of the few categories that actually stands to thrive in the agentic age,” Söderström tells investors. “This is because agents excel at replacing and taking care of things people would rather not do. People love getting rid of chores. But entertainment is the opposite. Nobody asks an agent to ‘summarize a song’ for them.”
Instead of opening Spotify, searching for an artist, and building a playlist themselves, listeners could ask an AI assistant to do the work for them. They might want music for a run, a podcast about something they’ve been discussing with an AI, or an audiobook recap that picks up exactly where they left off.
Spotify wants to be the service those agents turn to, letting people discover music and interact with Spotify through conversations rather than just its own app. Notably, Spotify was the first music service to integrate with Meta’s Muse assistant, and it also integrates with ChatGPT and Claude.

articles.title: Fusion startup Helion is developing new semiconductors that could double output of its power plants | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Fusion startup Helion has been awarded $175 million in federal funding to research, develop, and manufacture advanced semiconductors and power electronics for its fusion power plants, the company announced on Thursday.
Currently, those devices lose about 5% to 10% of the electricity that flows through them. While those losses seem small, they can compound themselves in a complex system like Helion’s.
“If we can cut that loss in half, that’s actually twice the power output of the fusion system,” David Kirtley, co-founder and CEO at Helion, told TechCrunch.
Helion has been racing to complete its first power plant, Orion, in time to meet a 2028 deadline to provide Microsoft with electricity from the grid. Funding from the award will help Helion build automated semiconductor module, packaging, and testing capacity to supply the fusion machine that’s currently under construction.
The new production line, to be built in Washington State, will be the first in the U.S. to make a class of semiconductor that is used not just in fusion power, but in manufacturing, wastewater treatment, medicine, and defense.
“There are no U.S. manufacturers right now that do it,” Kirtley said. “This is absolutely enabling going from zero to 100 for advanced, high-voltage, and pulsed semiconductors here in the United States.”

articles.title: Big Tech’s thirst for water is sparking a global resistance
articles.summary:
After ChatGPT was released in November 2022, the tech industry was quick to herald the chatbot as the marker of a new wave of technological progress. As companies pushed to create more powerful AI models, the water demand of their ambitions took a while to become clear. In April 2023, a research paper out of the University of California estimated that training the large language model behind the initial version of ChatGPT had required 185,000 gallons of water. For every extended conversation someone had with the chatbot or every time they asked it to write an email, they were effectively pouring a bottle of water down the drain.
That statistic got a lot of play when it was released. It became an early warning sign of what was coming as companies pushed chatbots as a universal technology that could replace psychologists, educators, lawyers, and even people’s friends or partners.
As public concern grew, Google and OpenAI came out with their own figures. The companies suggested that querying one of their chatbots used mere drops of water. Independent researchers were not impressed, arguing the companies were taking a narrow view of the water use necessary to power and cool increasingly monstrous data centers. Those water demands can be quite significant too.
A hyperscale data center can suck up between 1 and 5 million gallons of water a day, comparable to the amount used by a city of 10,000 to 50,000 people — depending on the part of the world we’re talking about. Consider how t…

articles.title: Investors break down how founders can raise a Series A today | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
In today’s market, no single metric defines what a Series A is, or how to raise one. At this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt, three investors offered founders advice on raising one, and one of them tacked on a warning. With money pouring into AI and revenue numbers being inflated to justify sky-high valuations, a correction could come as soon as 2027.
The warning came from Shailendra Singh, a managing director at Peak XV, who spoke alongside Jahanvi Sardana, a partner at Index Ventures, and Janelle Teng Wade, a partner at Bessemer. “Seed and venture, I’ve never seen it as dysfunctional as it is now,” Singh said, adding that the current market is one of the hardest to raise in that he has seen.
“The burden is high to convince any top firm that you are amongst the few special companies that can break out, and then the dispersion is very high on the terms you might get, how much capital you can raise, and what terms you can raise it,” he continued. In fact, it’s common now to see a company trying to close a round with as many as three different prices at once. “[I]’s a crazy sign of market froth,” he said.
“We’re calling it the ‘tranchopalooza,’” Sardana added, referring to the way rounds are being split into tranches, or separate chunks.

articles.title: Meta Ordered to Pay New Mexico $25 Billion for Deceiving Users About Privacy on Facebook
articles.summary:
A judge on Wednesday ordered Meta to pay New Mexico $25 billion after a jury found the company liable for deceiving users about privacy on Facebook, marking the biggest fine ever against the tech giant.
Facebook’s deception was intentional and executives consistently misled users about how the platform worked, state District Court Judge Francis J. Mathew wrote in his ruling.
“Facebook promised users that they (the users) controlled their data. This was false,” he said.
Jurors in September found Meta liable for over 43 million violations of New Mexico consumer protection laws for making misleading public statements about how it handled users’ personal data. The case was brought after political consulting firm Cambridge Analytica harvested Facebook data to generate targeted political ads during the 2016 election season.
The award will serve as a warning to tech companies that New Mexico will hold them accountable, state Attorney General Raúl Torrez said at a news conference.
“This judgment should be a signal, an unambiguous message, to Silicon Valley,” he said.
Meta said the ruling and Torrez’s office’s approach to enforcement “makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico.”
“At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online. We are confident we will prevail on appeal,” C.J. Mahoney, the company’s chief legal officer, said in a statement.

Advanced packaging growth and capacity constraints are pushing more onto OSATs.
Key Takeaways:
Foundries and outsourced assembly and test (OSAT) houses have traditionally had distinct lanes, but the lines are blurring as OSATs acquire select foundry capabilities and foundries return some of the jobs they have taken from OSATs.
“We’re at this bridging point where the IDMs and the foundries are doing more of what OSATs can do, and the OSATs are also trying to get much closer to what the foundry does at the back end,” said Raghu Nayak, head of sales at Zeiss.
OSATs will never compete with foundries on advanced nodes and front-end wafer fabrication. But for backend activities, where dimensions aren’t as demanding, OSATs are acquiring capabilities that replicate what foundries can do. The biggest areas of overlap are 2.5D integration and panel assembly, with hybrid bonding likely to move there as well.
The change affects equipment and materials. “We are seeing the migration of lithography-related materials and processes from traditional wafer fabs into advanced packaging environments,” said Poupak Khodabandeh, chief business officer at Brewer Science. “As advanced packaging increasingly relies on fine-pitch redistribution layers (RDLs), OSATs and packaging organizations are using materials and process flows that historically would have been associated with wafer fabrication.”

Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: What Breaks When Packaging Moves From Wafer To Panel?
articles.summary:
Engineers are discovering many things they thought were process assumptions were actually wafer assumptions.
Key Takeaways:
Moving advanced packaging from wafer to panel sounds, at first, like a geometry problem. Large AI and HPC packages are increasingly rectangular, while the 300mm wafer underneath them is still round. As the package size grows, more of that expensive processing ends up around the circle’s edges where nothing useful can be built.
A panel gives that area back. It can fit more large packages into the same process cycle, and unlike a wafer, its dimensions don’t impose the same hard limit on the size of a square or rectangular package. For advanced packages that keep getting larger, the economics are difficult to ignore.
But the semiconductor packaging sector has spent decades learning how to process wafers, not panels. Equipment, materials, recipes, handling systems, and process controls were all developed around the geometry and mechanical behavior of a round workpiece.
“The risk of doing the assembly on the 600mm panel is high, and I don’t think we have all the equipment today to run the process,” said Teck Chong Lee, technical director of advanced fan-out development for HPC applications at ASE, in a recent presentation. “One of the options is, once you complete the interposer in large format in 600, then you divide it into four pieces to run the assembly and the C4 process. This is a much lower-risk approach.”

articles.title: UN says we're going to blow past 1.5º warming, offers a "now what?" answer
articles.summary:
In 2015, all but two countries agreed to make an effort to keep global temperatures from reaching 1.5° C above pre-industrial readings. Since then, most of the world has largely treated what they signed on to as aspirational, and one of the largest emitters (the US) has alternately withdrawn and recommitted to the agreement. Meanwhile, the planet has responded as expected to steadily rising carbon emissions and appears to be practically at the 1.5° limit.
On Wednesday, for the first time, the United Nations Environmental Programme (UNEP) acknowledged that reality and conceded that the goal of keeping warming below 1.5° was no longer a viable one. Instead, its new goalposts focus on keeping both how long we exceed that limit and how much we exceed it by, at a minimum. Doing that will require both dramatic emissions cuts now and the removal of hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere before the century is out.
Bowing to the inevitable
Depending on which baseline you use to establish pre-industrial temperatures, as well as which reconstruction of global temperatures you rely on, the world has either gotten very close to, or already exceeded, the 1.5° milestone. The current El Niño event, which appears exceptionally strong, will almost certainly mean that we’ve gone over it no matter which records you choose.

articles.title: AI’s hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
articles.summary:
Sponsored
Provided byWD
Ask most executives to picture the cost of AI and they’ll likely see GPUs—racks of accelerators with gigawatts of power—and a waitlist for silicon. But that picture leaves something out: Data storage costs.
What happens to data after a model responds? Much of the back-end data that’s generated—from billions of daily prompts, images, and videos—needs to be stored. But data storage is one of the harder infrastructure costs to plan for, and it’s often overlooked in initial AI infrastructure planning.
As inference scales, the data footprint grows with it
Traditionally, AI infrastructure conversations have centered on the compute-intensive process of training a model. Training is finite: a run starts, burns through compute, and ends. But inference runs continuously, every time a model answers a prompt. For infrastructure planning, that difference matters: A training run is a project you can budget for and retire. Inference doesn’t retire; every inference request leaves something behind.
Take AI-generated video. In this workload, the back-end spend can be significant. From internal measurements, WD found that an 8-second clip (returned to a user as a 3.97MB 720p file) left more than 500MB of associated data behind on the back end, including logs, cached context, immediate renders, backups, and safety records. articles.title: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email

Unknown hackers hijacked more than 300 Tor exit nodes and reconfigured them to favor unencrypted email traffic and redirect SSH connections through servers they controlled, a researcher reported Tuesday.
The hijacking began in late August, when, according to Tor volunteers, the attacker used a valid password that had been reused to gain access to a Tor management server. The attacker then installed Ebury, a backdoor written for Linux that was discovered 12 years ago.
Mysteries remain
Then the attacker connected from the management server to a second Tor server, called Switzerland2, through SSH, using an RSA key that, for unknown reasons, investigators couldn’t find among Switzerland2’s authorized keys. articles.title: What does it actually mean to treat data as an asset?

What does it actually mean to treat data as an asset?
Turning data into a defined, governed and commercially usable asset
We understand what it means to own a house, a car, a share in a company, a patent or a trademark. In each case, there is an established legal framework that defines the asset, establishes who holds it and enables it to be sold, transferred, financed or protected.
Data is more complicated. A business may have spent decades building a valuable body of data that it protects and depends upon, yet establishing precisely what constitutes that asset, and what rights are attached to it, is far less straightforward.
That uncertainty has commercial consequences. It can make data harder to value, license or share with confidence, leaving transactions heavily dependent on contracts and trust between the parties rather than an independently verifiable understanding of what the data is and how it may be used.
Aga Strandskov, Head of Data Strategy, Digital Isle of Man
This is a challenge we have been exploring in the Isle of Man through the development of the Data Asset Foundations framework, which establishes the statutory basis for defined, governed data to be recognized as an asset.
With the framework now moving into implementation, a much broader question remains relevant for businesses: if we are serious about treating data as an asset, what does that actually require?
What makes data an asset?

articles.title: 480,000 phishing emails sent from a PC hidden behind a fridge in a Japanese hotel room — Chinese couple arrested over fraud operation, scammers remotely leech Wi-Fi to target 2.4 million victims
articles.summary:
480,000 phishing emails sent from a PC hidden behind a fridge in a Japanese hotel room — Chinese couple arrested over fraud operation, scammers remotely leech Wi-Fi to target 2.4 million victims
Police arrested a Chinese couple for placing the computer that was found in a Kobe hotel and using stolen credit cards to make purchases.
A computer, found hidden behind a fridge in a Japanese hotel room, was responsible for sending around 480,000 phishing emails, Hackread reports. The computer was placed there by a Chinese couple who lived locally, and the pair have now been arrested for both the hidden phishing PC and a separate slew of purchases that were made using stolen credit card details. Ye Jiafeng, 39, and his wife, Shen Qi, 39, now face multiple charges including fraudulent obstruction of business and trespass as well as computer fraud.
The scam began on 15 May, 2025, when Ye connected the computer to hotel Wi-Fi and then hid it behind a fridge. There it stayed, sending around 480,000 emails. When it was discovered, the machine had around 2.4 million email addresses, presumably just waiting to be phished. The emails claimed to be from credit card companies and sent unsuspecting recipients to fake websites in an attempt to capture their credit card information. It's believed that the computer was administered remotely, allowing it to remain in situ without any in-person maintenance required.

articles.title: Google turns the infrastructure behind Gemini’s agents into a cloud service
articles.summary:
Google turns the infrastructure behind Gemini’s agents into a cloud service
Google will soon make the infrastructure that powers its Gemini agents available to Google Cloud users in preview.
Announced on Thursday at the Linux Foundation’s AGNTCon+MCPCon in San Jose, Agent Compute Engine will become available in preview to Google Cloud users later this year. It will provide every AI agent with a hardware-isolated microVM that combines the speed of containers with the security of a sandbox.
Who else offers agent sandboxes?
The idea of agent sandboxes is anything but new, of course. Startups like E2B and Daytona offer them to developers (and support them on any cloud), as does AWS with Bedrock AgentCore.
E2B runs each sandbox in a Firecracker microVM, the open source virtualization technology AWS originally built for Lambda. It can pause a sandbox with its memory and filesystem intact and resume it in about a second. Daytona started out with containers but added microVM sandboxes in July. Those can pause a full machine or fork a running one into identical copies.
AgentCore also gives every agent session its own microVM. AWS doesn’t charge for CPU while an agent waits on a model or tool call, though memory keeps billing until the runtime reclaims it. Those sessions top out at eight hours. In August, AWS added EC2-based runtime instances that can keep shared sessions alive for up to 14 days.

articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.summary:
AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness

La empresa lo lanzó como prueba limitada, por lista de espera, para suscriptores pagos de Claude en Estados Unidos.

Claude Duet opera desde una computadora virtual con su propio navegador, por lo que puede seguir trabajando aunque el dispositivo del usuario esté apagado.
La aplicación está disponible como descarga independiente para iOS y Android, además de la versión web en claude.ai. articles.title: Africa's cloud infrastructure crisis risks exploitation
articles.summary:
Nigeria reportedly bleeds millions of dollars annually due to its reliance on cloud infrastructure controlled by a handful of foreign big tech firms, according to Melanie Hui, Chief Executive Officer of Luminate, a global organisation working to ensure digital technology serves human rights.
Delivering the keynote address at the Build 2026 Conference in Abuja on Wednesday, Hui warned that Africa risks being locked into a subordinate role in the global artificial intelligence economy unless the continent secures genuine ownership of the infrastructure powering the technology.
“My African friends tell me they will not be confined to the role of consumer, supplier of raw data, source of critical minerals or provider of low-paid labour in somebody else’s AI economy,” Hui told an audience of government officials, diplomats, tech leaders, and members of the Nigeria AI Collective. “And Luminate will stand with them in securing a better digital age.”
To illustrate her point, Hui referenced India’s Ministry of Agriculture, which leveraged AI to predict monsoon patterns for nearly 40 million farmers. Citing African energy expert Rose Mutiso, Hui noted that AI was merely “the last piece of this breakthrough, not the first.”
The initiative succeeded because key foundation layers were already in place: actionable demand from local farmers, public climate data, a century of local rainfall records, and an established SMS distribution network operating in native languages.

articles.title: Amazon lanza gafas inteligentes para conductores
articles.summary:
Las gafas inteligentes de Amazon ayudarán a sus repartidores a encontrar los paquetes y llevarlos hasta la puerta del cliente. Además, podrán tomar miles de fotografías de personas y propiedades durante una jornada laboral. La segunda función está llamando la atención, ya que se basa en unas declaraciones de Viraj Chatterjee, el responsable de Amazon del proyecto.
El anuncio inicial sobre los dispositivos se produjo el 22 de octubre de 2025. La expansión prevista sí corresponde a 2026: Amazon anuncia 5.000 dispositivos adicionales, con el objetivo de superar los 20.000 para finales de 2027. Se trata de planes futuros, así que esas cifras no representan a repartidores que ya hayan recibido las gafas.
Las capturas descritas por la información que ha vuelto a llamar la atención se producirían mientras el repartidor camina. Se habla de fotografías probablemente cada pocos segundos, para que personas las revisen y después se incorporen a Wellspring, el sistema de inteligencia artificial (IA) de Amazon para sus mapas de navegación de reparto. La empresa “se encamina sin darse cuenta hacia otra polémica por invasión de la privacidad”, afirmó el columnista de tecnología Dave Lee.
Amazon se ha defendido de este coro de críticas. “La idea de que Amazon utilice gafas inteligentes de reparto como una forma de vigilancia distorsiona la tecnología y su propósito”, declaró la portavoz Leigh Anne Gullett. articles.title: BioWare ayudó a definir el rol occidental y la inclusión en videojuegos, pero no cabe en la nueva EA propiedad de Arabia Saudí
articles.summary:
Electronic Arts está construyendo su próximo capítulo y, por eso, ha cerrado BioWare. El estudio canadiense que nació hace 30 años y ayudó a definir el rol occidental con sagas como 'Baldur's Gate', 'Star Wars: Caballeros de la Última República', 'Dragon Age' o 'Mass Effect', ha echado la persiana como parte de una profunda reestructuración en EA, la empresa matriz, que ha recortado unos 400 empleos.
La decisión llega dos meses y medio después de que la compañía pasara a manos de un consorcio liderado por el fondo soberano saudí. Y no por esperada, deja de ser una noticia triste.
Qué ha pasado. Si te has criado con alguno de los títulos de BioWare, la noticia pegó como un camión la tarde de este miércoles 21 de octubre. Cam Weber (presidente y director de estudios de EA) y David Tinson (presidente y director de operaciones) enviaron una carta a la plantilla en la que anunciaban el cierre del último estudio que quedaba a BioWare, el de Edmonton.
Reconocen que es un estudio legendario y que no han tomado la decisión a la ligera, pero que había un pequeño grupo de personas (se habla de unos 50 desarrolladores) trabajando aún en las fases iniciales de un nuevo 'Mass Effect' y que, ahora, desde EA habían tomado la decisión de no seguir adelante. Como decíamos, según Bloomberg es parte de un plan de despidos de 400 empleados, alrededor de un 3% de la plantilla de EA, aunque esto no ha sido confirmado por la compañía.

articles.title: Cisco Patches 34 Vulnerabilities Across Multiple Products
articles.summary:
Cisco on Wednesday announced patches for 34 vulnerabilities across Expressway Series, IOS XR, Snort 3, and Unified Communications products.
Expressway Series received fixes for 10 vulnerabilities, including a critical-severity remote code execution (RCE) bug tracked as CVE-2026-76466.
According to Cisco, the use of persistent cookies and insufficient validation of client certificates in certain configurations could allow attackers to connect to the database service and invoke specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands to exploit the bug.
“A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device,” Cisco notes.
The security defect was patched in Expressway Series version X15.5.20, which also resolves eight CVEs that group multiple vulnerabilities under their specific CWE category. A medium-severity information disclosure bug was also fixed.
Cisco patched nine CVEs in Unified Communications products, including Emergency Responder, Prime Collaboration Deployment, Unified Communications Manager (CM), Unified Communications Manager IM & Presence Service (CM IM&P), Unified Communications Manager Session Management Edition (CM SME), and Unity Connection.
The most severe are CVE-2026-76473, CVE-2026-76474, and CVE-2026-76475, three critical-severity issues that group multiple improper resource control, improper authentication, and improper input neutralization holes.

articles.title: Comme WhatsApp, ChatGPT met enfin vos conversations sous clé
articles.summary:
OpenAI déploie depuis le 20 octobre les « conversations verrouillées » dans ChatGPT, du compte gratuit aux offres Enterprise et Edu. Le dispositif rappelle le verrouillage des discussions que WhatsApp propose depuis le 15 mai 2023 : un code à quatre chiffres, ou Face ID et Touch ID sur mobile, et le fil disparaît des écrans. La fonction, repérée dès le mois d’août dans le code de l’application Android, arrive progressivement sur le web, les téléphones et les applications de bureau.
Un dossier sous code, invisible dans l’historique
Une fois verrouillée, la conversation rejoint un espace dédié et s’efface de l’historique, des fils épinglés et des résultats de recherche. L’ouvrir réclame le code, ou la biométrie du téléphone, et un geste suffit ensuite pour rendre le fil à la circulation générale. Le dossier « Conversations verrouillées » reste visible dans l’interface. WhatsApp propose depuis fin 2023 un code secret qui masque jusqu’à l’existence du dossier, un cran de discrétion encore hors de portée de ChatGPT. Le déploiement s’étalant sur plusieurs semaines, l’option peut d’ailleurs encore manquer à l’appel sur certains comptes.
Les conversations temporaires, les archives, les discussions de groupe ou celles liées à une tâche programmée restent hors du périmètre. articles.title: Authorities disrupt nearly 11,000 cybercrime networks in Africa
articles.summary:
Law enforcement agencies have disrupted nearly 11,000 cybercriminal networks and arrested more than 1,400 people in Operation Serengeti III, which targeted business email compromise, ransomware, and online scams.
Coordinated by Interpol, the operation involved authorities from 21 countries and private partners like Team Cymru, Kaspersky, Group-IB, and Fortinet, in a major crackdown on cybercrime across Africa.
The action unrolled between June 29 and August 31 and led to the recovery of more than $105 million in illegal funds.
In a press release today, Interpol says that Operation Serengeti III has resulted in the arrest of 1,462 suspected cybercriminals and the dismantling of 10,909 malicious networks.
The investigation identified 65,929 victims and estimated financial losses at more than $385 million.
In Uganda, law enforcement dismantled two transnational fraud rings and arrested 365 individuals for suspected links to online investment and pension fraud operations.
Another highlight of the operation are illegal cryptocurrency mining centers in Angola, where nine suspects have been arrested, and more than 2,000 mining devices have been seized.
Authorities also arrested one individual in Nigeria, suspected of running "a large-scale phishing and business email compromise operation that harvested software credentials and amassed approximately 2.1 million email addresses."

articles.title: Deepx Building Open Software Ecosystem to Scale Physical AI Beyond the Data Center - EE Times
articles.summary:
The next competitive battle in edge AI may not be decided by TOPS alone, according to Lokwon Kim, founder and CEO of Deepx, in an interview with EE Times Asia. The more consequential question, he said, is whether AI semiconductor companies can make their technology easy to develop, deploy, and scale.`
That does not make silicon less important. Kim’s view is that hardware remains the entry point, but software and ecosystem support determine whether a technical advantage becomes a sustainable commercial position.
Deepx has built its strategy around this distinction as it shifts from developing low-power AI accelerators to building a broader platform for physical AI. The company is connecting its neural processing units (NPUs) to existing model frameworks, development platforms, and embedded systems rather than building an entirely closed software stack.
The strategy reflects a broader challenge facing physical AI. Unlike cloud AI, where developers can often work within relatively standardized computing environments, physical AI must operate across cameras, robots, vehicles, drones, industrial equipment, and other systems with widely different power, thermal, sensor, operating-system, and real-time requirements.
For Deepx, that fragmentation has become one of the biggest barriers to moving AI projects beyond proof of concept.

articles.title: How Self-Aligned CFET Technology Could Extend CMOS Scaling Beyond 10 Å
articles.summary:
A process sequence for SRAM and logic that delivers higher performance through larger effective channel width and improved electrostatics at smaller nodes.
As their dimensions continue to shrink, conventional gate-all-around (GAA) nanosheet transistors may face growing challenges, such as leakage, mobility, resistance, and manufacturing variability.
A proposed self-aligned complementary field-effect transistor (SA-CFET) architecture addresses these constraints by vertically stacking N-channel metal-oxide-semiconductor (NMOS) and P-channel metal-oxide-semiconductor (PMOS) devices and using self-aligned modules to improve density and manufacturability.
A complementary field-effect transistor (CFET) is a transistor architecture that vertically stacks NMOS and PMOS devices. This configuration can reduce cell area, increase effective channel width, and improve electrostatic control compared with side-by-side device layouts.
With SEMulator3D, the Semiverse Solutions team used digital twin process modeling to show that the self-aligned architecture can support static random-access memory (SRAM) and logic cells while delivering a 0.0094 μm² SRAM bit cell, a 52.7% area reduction compared with N3 technology, and at least a 10 nm overlay window across critical contact layers.

articles.summary:
Everspin Technologies is looking to expand its magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) beyond established industrial applications into AI servers, data centers, and satellite systems, as AI workloads increase demand for faster, persistent memory.

Meta turns Muse sharing back on
Meta has given new URLs to shared Muse ‘artifacts’ after security researchers reported that public links could be easy to find.
Researchers at Claroc reported earlier this week that Muse the web addresses for shared conversations from Muse were named after a conversation’s title and written into public DNS. Ars Technica said Tuesday that Meta paused the sharing feature after it reached out about what was going on.
In a post today on X, Meta’s David Singleton says that “The underlying issue is now fixed, and sharing is back on.” According to Singleton, the issue was with URLs for shared Muse artifacts, which Meta says are things like documents and images inside Muse, and wasn’t a flaw with chat sharing.
“If you shared an artifact before the fix: it now has a new URL,” Singleton says. “Anyone visiting the old link will see a note asking them to get the new one from you. We know that’s a pain, and we’re sorry for the disruption — but protecting user data has to come first.”

A primer on this crucial and frankly mysterious piece of climate science.
How much do you know about permafrost?
Maybe, like me, you’ve been aware that this layer of frozen soil is thawing, that it’s important in the global puzzle of climate change … and that’s about the extent of it.
The great news for both of us is that my colleague James Temple just published two in-depth stories about permafrost. His reporting took him to the boreal forests of Alaska, where he helicoptered into the wilderness to learn more about how this material could affect our climate both now and in the future.
I’d recommend you give both of James’s stories a read. There’s this feature about efforts to tackle the intensifying fires that are threatening permafrost, as well as this look at how researchers are trying to understand the complicated tangle of potential climate effects. Here are three things I took away.
Permafrost is a massive blind spot for climate change
Permafrost is the frozen layer of soil that’s under about 15% of land around the Northern Hemisphere. While technically material needs to be frozen for only two consecutive years to count as permafrost, most of our current permafrost formed during the last ice age.

articles.title: Stop guessing auto scaling targets for TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services

Artificial Intelligence
Stop guessing auto scaling targets for TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI
A traffic spike hits your self-hosted text-to-speech (TTS) endpoint, and requests start queueing. Latency climbs past your service level objective (SLO) right when the most callers are listening. The auto scaling policy behind that endpoint was supposed to prevent this, but the target value it scales on was a guess, and guesses like that fail silently until real traffic proves them wrong.
Get that number wrong, and it’s paid for in one of two ways, and neither shows up as an alarm. Guess too conservative, and the fleet runs GPU instances that sit mostly idle. That cost lands on every invoice but never trips an incident report. Guess too aggressive, and the fleet carries a risk nobody sees. Each instance holds more concurrent requests than it can serve inside its latency promise. Nothing looks wrong until a real traffic spike pushes queueing time past the SLO. That happens right when the most callers are listening. That’s the hidden gap. A policy that looks fine on the console can already be failing the people it’s supposed to serve.
In this post, we deploy Kokoro-82M, an 82-million-parameter TTS model, as a custom container on an Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoint. AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) stacks handle the deployment. We replace guesswork with two measurements taken against the live endpoint. ¿En serio es necesario todo esto? A veces, en ciencia, no basta con sentarse y mirar. A veces, la única forma que tenemos de averiguar qué pasa es experimentando. Este es un caso paradigmático: ya sabíamos que las marismas frenan el oleaje; lo que no teníamos ni idea es de su aguante frente a tormentas de verdad. Tormentas como las que se generan en el tipo de canales que utilizan en la Universidad de Delft.
No es la primera vez que se hace, claro. En 2013, unos investigadores llevaron bloques de una marisma similar al gran canal de Hannover. On parle beaucoup de PHP ces temps-ci, non sans raison : le langage qui est derrière une multitude de sites web est victime de deux failles de sécurité très graves. Heureusement, des correctifs ont été déployés le 21 octobre 2026 et ils sont maintenant en cours d’installation ; si vous avez un site sous WordPress, il est facile de vérifier sa version PHP.
Toute cette affaire est l’occasion de faire un bref pas de côté, pour faire un petit point de culture générale en informatique, car PHP est un acronyme qui a historiquement deux significations. Il existe en effet une explication officielle, ainsi qu’un sens historique.
Quand on demande à la foire aux questions du site officiel PHP.net ce que veut dire PHP, la réponse a tout l’air d’une vanne de développeur : « PHP : Hypertext Preprocessor », soit un préprocesseur hypertexte, c’est-à-dire un programme informatique qui fabrique les pages web avant de les envoyer au navigateur, pour les afficher à l’internaute.
Sauf que le premier mot du sigle est le sigle lui-même, ce qui embrouille beaucoup de monde, reconnaît la documentation.
En fait, c’est ce qu’on appelle un acronyme récursif. On retrouve ce même clin d’œil chez GNU, le projet de système d’exploitation libre dont le nom signifie « GNU’s Not Unix ». C’est l’exemple le plus connu, mais on en trouve d’autres, comme l’émulateur WINE, dont le nom signifie… « Wine Is Not an Emulator ».

articles.title: AI agent security is a lifecycle — not a gatekeeper
articles.summary:
AI agent security is a lifecycle — not a gatekeeper
Enterprise security has traditionally operated on a relatively straightforward premise: establish identity, authenticate the requester, determine what that identity can access, and enforce those permissions.
AI agents introduce a fundamental complication. They don’t simply access systems. They interpret objectives, select tools, create sub-agents, make decisions, and execute actions, often using credentials and permissions inherited from humans.
The problem isn’t necessarily that an agent lacks proper credentials. It’s that those credentials may authorize actions the human never intended the agent to perform. And unlike conventional software, agents can change their execution paths dynamically in pursuit of an objective.
“The problem isn’t necessarily that an agent lacks proper credentials. It’s that those credentials may authorize actions the human never intended the agent to perform.”
This creates a new operational requirement: security must evaluate not only who or what is acting, but what an agent is attempting to do, on whose authority, and under which policy. Meeting that requirement takes more than a security checkpoint. It requires a continuous agent security lifecycle.
Defense-in-depth needs action-level authorization

Google’s tensor processing units (TPUs) — its custom AI chips — now serve AI in production at Meta (creator of the widely used PyTorch AI framework) through a new PyTorch-native version of the SGLang inference engine, announced on Google’s developer blog. A matching version of vLLM, another widely used inference engine, was also announced as open source.
Previously, both engines used Google’s own JAX AI framework to run on TPUs. The new versions allow the hardware to be a native option for PyTorch, mostly without rewriting.
“SGLang-TorchTPU is running in production at Meta today” after “a close three-way collaboration between Meta, Google, and the SGLang team,” said Meta’s PyTorch-TPU lead Zongwei Zhou. That team works at RadixArk, a startup founded by SGLang’s creators, which built the engine with Google and Meta. The engine, he said, gives Meta “a remarkably mature, PyTorch-native serving stack.”
Jana van Greunen, director of PyTorch engineering at Meta, added in Google’s TorchTPU post that Meta “cannot be constrained by a single hardware architecture” and that TorchTPU “enables us to deploy our PyTorch workloads to Google TPUs.” Google said it co-developed TorchTPU with Meta’s PyTorch team.

articles.title: New Serious PHP Vulnerabilities Released and Patched - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
New Serious PHP Vulnerabilities Released and Patched
PHP maintainers have released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities:
PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately.
Who is at risk: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.
The vulnerabilities:
- RCE via OOM corruption, CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w): out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid.
- RCE via stale global state, CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp): request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it.
Updating PHP is the only way to regain security. Do it now.

The vast impact of the bugs, uncovered with the help of OpenAI and Google models after being undetected for more than a decade, highlights the ability of AI to upend cybersecurity.

articles.title: Chinese hackers spied on thousands of companies after breaching IT giant ConnectWise | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The bad week for cybersecurity just got worse for thousands more companies, who were spied on by Chinese hackers following the breach of IT management and remote access giant ConnectWise.
Security researchers at Microsoft say the China state-aligned hackers broke into ConnectWise’s cloud backup service and stole application credentials that are used to establish data links between ConnectWise and its corporate customers, who rely on the cloud service to back up their company’s data.
By stealing the credentials, the hackers could log in to the customer’s Microsoft-hosted environment as if they were an authorized user and access their emails and other files.
According to Microsoft, the hackers used AI agents to rapidly hack into around 2,250 organizations at a rate of almost 3,000 attempted sign-ins per minute. Microsoft said this speed gives defenders “little time to detect and respond.”
The speed of the mass-hacks was attributed to the use of AI agents, specifically ARTEX, an open source AI framework that works with AI models to stress-test cyber defenses. The same AI software was used in a recent compromise of South Korea’s financial systems, many of which had weak security and lacked multi-factor authentication.
ConnectWise said it’s paused access to its cloud backup system and is investigating the breach. As of Thursday, the company said it was working on restoring the service.

A customer asks an AI voice agent a question and waits. The agent already has an answer, it’s midway through generating a long, multi-paragraph response, but the customer hears nothing for five seconds. By the time an answer arrives, the customer is frustrated, confused, and no longer paying attention.
Text-to-speech integrations create exactly that gap. A one-sentence response might generate in 600 milliseconds, but the full response takes five seconds, and the integration waits for all of it before synthesis starts.
This post shows how to close that gap. We stream each sentence to a hosted Kokoro-82M text-to-speech (TTS) model on Amazon SageMaker AI as soon as an agent produces it, so synthesis begins on sentence one instead of the finished response. Solution overview
This solution closes the gap by streaming synthesis alongside generation instead of waiting for it to finish. As the agent produces each sentence, that sentence streams immediately to a hosted Kokoro-82M text-to-speech model, so audio playback can start before the agent finishes speaking its full response. articles.title: PVTW: Extending Silicon Characterization From PVT To Real-World Workload
articles.summary:
Two devices operating at exactly the same voltage, frequency, and temperature can behave differently depending on what they are being asked to do.
For decades, silicon characterization has been built around Process, Voltage, and Temperature, or PVT. We characterize devices across process variation, sweep voltage and frequency, control temperature, generate SHMOO plots, and establish the operating envelope of the silicon.
That methodology remains fundamental. But today’s high-performance processors are increasingly systems in their own right. An AI accelerator may contain thousands of compute elements, distributed SRAM, high-speed SerDes, PCIe and Ethernet interfaces, multiple clock and power domains, advanced packaging, firmware, operating systems, compilers and application software.
This suggests adding another dimension: PVTW: Process × Voltage × Temperature × Workload
Frequency can be swept within this characterization space to determine operating margin.
The objective is not to replace traditional ATE characterization with System Level Test. It is to combine the electrical precision and control available from ATE with the realistic operating environment available from SLT, while retaining the ability to use either independently.
One way to implement PVTW is through a hybrid characterization architecture integrating ATE resources and SLT capability.

articles.title: Who on-calls an AI? This is the unresolved crisis of agent ownership

Who on-calls an AI? This is the unresolved crisis of agent ownership
At 2:07 a.m., an AI agent starts failing.
The application is still running, but requests are timing out because a downstream API is returning errors. The agent has already retried twice, using more tokens than usual, and its response time has roughly doubled.
The first question should not be:
	“Which model should we use?”
It should be:
	“Who owns this system right now?”
That question is easy to overlook when building AI agents. Teams often pour effort into prompts, retrieval, tools, and model selection, but production ownership determines whether an agent becomes a dependable service or another source of operational risk.
“Teams often pour effort into prompts, retrieval, tools, and model selection, but production ownership determines whether an agent becomes a dependable service or another source of operational risk.”
A production agent needs an owner, boundaries, telemetry, failure policies, escalation paths, and a clear distinction between what the system may automate and what requires human intervention.
A production agent should not have a direct path from reasoning to action. Each tool invocation should pass through explicit controls, remain observable, and have a defined path to human intervention.
Here’s a practical way to build those controls.
Step 1: Treat the agent as a production service
An agent should have the same operational identity as any other production service.

articles.title: Laut einer Studie hält ein Drittel der Führungskräfte KI für schlauer als sich selbst: Was bedeutet das für Unternehmen?
articles.summary:
Cognitive Offloading: Wie KI das Urteilsvermögen von Führungskräften untergräbt
Rund ein Drittel der Führungskräfte gibt an, KI mehr zu vertrauen als dem eigenen Urteilsvermögen. Bei Angestellten auf niedrigeren Positionen ist das nur etwa halb so häufig der Fall. Das geht aus einer Umfrage des Forschungs- und Medienunternehmens Charter hervor. Im August wurden dafür über 5.000 Personen in den USA befragt, die angaben, KI bei der Arbeit zu nutzen. Für Unternehmen entsteht aus dieser Begeisterung ein großes Problem: Sie stellen Führungskräfte wegen ihrer Erfahrung und ihres Wissens ein – nicht, um Entscheidungen an KI zu übergeben.
Führungskräfte lagern Denkprozesse aus
Immer mehr Menschen nutzen KI, um E-Mails vorzuformulieren, Präsentationen zu erstellen oder die Entscheidungsfindung zu beschleunigen. Dafür gibt es sogar einen eigenen Begriff: „Cognitive Offloading“. Er bezeichnet die Tendenz, Denkarbeit an ein KI-System auszulagern, um die eigene geistige Belastung zu verringern. articles.title: LTO roadmap extends to 365 TB per cartridge as tape storage refuses to die — AI boom spurs relevance of cheap, airgapped storage
articles.summary:
LTO roadmap extends to 365 TB per cartridge as tape storage refuses to die —25-year-old format sees 400x capacity increase without changing form factor
HPE, IBM, and Quantum will keep developing LTO as demand booms.
In a world where SSDs with up to 256TB capacity are about to enter the scene to compete against hard disk drives that store over 40TB, magnetic tape storage may seem archaic. However, the 25-year-old Linear Tape-Open (LTO) format continues to evolve at a rather impressive pace.
The current LTO-10 generation stores up to 40TB of uncompressed data per cartridge, while HPE, IBM, and Quantum — the companies behind the LTO Program — now envision LTO-14 cartridges with up to 365TB of native capacity. But capacity is not the only advantage of LTO. In fact, the consortium has deliberately slowed its capacity roadmap in a bid to prioritize reliability, cost per terabyte, and manageable backup and recovery times over the previous goal of doubling capacity with every generation.
LTO began in 2000 with the LTO-1 format, which stored just 100GB of data natively and transferred it at 20 MB/s. Since then, capacity increased to 200GB with LTO-2, 400GB with LTO-3, 800GB with LTO-4, 1.5TB with LTO-5, 2.5TB with LTO-6, 6TB with LTO-7, 12TB with LTO-8, and 18TB with LTO-9.
The original LTO-10 media introduced in 2025 increased native capacity to 30TB, whereas an extended-length LTO-10 cartridge announced later increased it further to 40TB.

articles.title: This emulator reimagines Nintendo’s Virtual Boy with a full color display

Last year, we reported on Red Viper, a Virtual Boy emulator that added a splash of Super Game Boy-style color to Nintendo’s famously failed red-on-black “portable” 3D headset from the ’90s. Now, a new emulation experiment, VBoy Color, has taken the concept to a higher level, using a tile-based palette system that allows for many more distinct colors in each individual Virtual Boy frame.
Rather than simply replacing the Virtual Boy’s four shades of red with four different colors, VBoy Color’s readme files explain how the emulator’s game-specific Color Packs can assign a distinct four-color palette to each 8×8 tile in a Virtual Boy scene. That means the emulator can differentiate between green pipes, grey platforms, and red brick wall in Mario Clash, for instance, even though all those in-game objects share the same overlapping red hues in the original game.
The Game Boy Color-esque results feel like being transported into an alternate history where Nintendo invested in a full-color display rather than cheaper red LEDs for the Virtual Boy hardware. The increased contrast between differently colored elements is particularly welcome in games like Jack Bros. or Vertical Force, where the original red-on-red display often makes it hard to differentiate the player-character from busy red background elements.

AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load.
The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production.
Delivering a Dynamic View of an AI Factory
Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation. Minerva connects those signals across NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and workloads.
With these signals, Minerva builds a dynamic knowledge graph that logically maps the infrastructure — GPUs, SuperNICs, switches and cables — and the jobs running on it. This context helps operators trace a slow training job to the component affecting it, even across a factory with hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

articles.title: Signal Vulnerability Lets Malicious Callers Block Hang-Ups
articles.summary:
Signal has resolved a critical-severity vulnerability that could allow a malicious caller to keep audio and video tracks enabled even after the user hung up.
The security defect is tracked as CVE-2026-113380 (CVSS score of 9.3) and impacts RingRTC, the open source library Signal uses for voice and video calls, which is based on WebRTC.
Due to the issue, a remote peer could flood the call’s Finite State Machine (FSM) event queue with junk, and the call would not terminate.
This happened because the hangup was not treated as a kill switch, but as an event added to the FSM event queue; there was no rate limit on peer-originated events; and the hangup event had no priority.
“Flood the queue with junk and the hang-up waits behind attacker noise forever, so the call (microphone, possibly camera) is never torn down,” a GitHub write-up by a researcher reads.
By exploiting the vulnerability, an attacker could keep the audio and video tracks flowing from a target device while the victim believes they ended the call.
The security defect was resolved in RingRTC version 2.72.0, which was released on September 4.
Details on the flaw, however, were published on Tuesday, along with a conceptual proof-of-concept (PoC). NIST added the CVE to the NVD database on Tuesday.
Signal resolved the issue by ensuring that call termination requests do not remain blocked in FSM’s event queue and are detected independently.
Users should update their Signal applications as soon as possible. Otherwise, they …

articles.title: Harbor Adds Docker Sandboxes to Run Reproducible AI Agent Evals in Isolated MicroVMs
articles.summary:
Docker announced that Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, now works with Docker Sandboxes. This change allows each evaluation task to run in its own microVM. So, instead of sharing a container, tasks are isolated for better performance. The same tasks run locally or in Docker Cloud Sandboxes, and Docker says it has tested Harbor with 64 concurrent tasks in the cloud.
Evaluating a coding agent means letting it install packages, edit files, and run commands, and a benchmark repeats this thousands of times. Docker's engineers describe this as running untrusted, AI-written code at scale. They also flag reward hacking, where an agent earns a passing score by tampering with tests or overwriting the file that records its score instead of solving the task. Harbor manages orchestration. It runs tasks, collects scores, and logs. It also supports benchmarks like Terminal-Bench. It needs an execution environment that is both isolated and consistent.
Each task runs in a Docker Sandbox, a microVM with its own kernel, so agent activity stays inside the VM and cannot reach the host, other tasks, or anything outside the environment. In Docker Cloud Sandboxes, configurable network policies let a task pull dependencies during setup, then restrict internet access while the agent works. Every agent is then evaluated under the same network conditions, which addresses a common source of non-reproducible results. Docker Compose is supported, so Harbor can run multi-container tasks in…

Did one of your favorite websites go dark on Wednesday? Some did, as operators took services offline while they waited for fixes to two critical flaws in PHP, the language behind much of the web.
The precaution didn’t mean those sites were hacked. The holes themselves were bad news with a capital B. But the bigger long-term concern might be how the embargo on the patches was handled.
PHP powers roughly 70% of websites, but that figure describes PHP’s reach, not the number of vulnerable or compromised sites.

The flaws are CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The PHP project’s fixed releases are 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12; users of older PHP branches need a supported upgrade or a distributor’s backport.
The PHP security emergency, aka PHP2Shell, exposed more than dangerous bugs in a widely used language. The release also set off a dispute over coordinated disclosure and underscored the pressure on open-source maintainers as AI-assisted researchers find and develop exploits faster.
The road to this emergency ran through OpenAI’s Patch the Planet initiative. Healthcare organizations want the same thing from AI that every other business wants: faster answers, less manual work, and insights that reach decision-makers in time to act on them. Protected Health Information (PHI) is any information that identifies a person and relates to their health, care, or payment for care, such as a medical note, a claim, or a member ID. Agentic AI changes what it means for software to “touch PHI.” A traditional analytics tool reads data and returns a response. An agentic workspace like Amazon Quick might go further. Fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) today usually forces a tradeoff between training loop control and operational simplicity. With fully managed services you select a base model, provide data and hyperparameters, and the service owns everything else, which works well when a standard, prepackaged recipe fits your problem. Less managed services give you more control, but you also manage more of the underlying infrastructure and training frameworks. Sometimes a standard recipe isn’t enough: you need a custom loss or data curriculum for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), your own preference optimization, a reinforcement learning (RL) reward function, or an alignment algorithm published last week. As soon as you need to shape the training procedure yourself, you take on that infrastructure work to gain algorithmic freedom.
Today, serverless model customization in Amazon SageMaker AI expands with training session APIs, which remove that tradeoff by drawing the abstraction boundary one level lower. Instead of abstracting away the algorithm, they abstract away the compute. Operations like forward_backward(), optim_step(), and sample() become SageMaker API calls that you compose into whatever procedure your technique requires: SFT, preference optimization, RL, or something new. articles.title: LiteLLM release pipeline hacked to distribute info-stealer malware
articles.summary:
Hackers compromised the LiteLLM project’s PyPI package and published malicious Docker images with a payload that steals credentials, secrets, and environment variables.
The supply-chain attack affected all PyPI wheels (.whl installation packages) for LiteLLM version 1.107.0, impacting Windows, Linux, and macOS systems.
LiteLLM is an open-source Python SDK and AI gateway that enables applications to access AI models from different providers through a common API.
It is a massively popular project with 61,800 GitHub stars, 92 million monthly downloads on PyPI, and is used by high-profile companies like NVIDIA, Netflix, AT&T, and Okta.
The project says that the release pipeline was compromised on October 21 and a threat actor pushed version 1.107.0 to the Docker registry and PyPI.
"This version contained compiled malware which steals credentials and loads remote-code execution tools," the maintainer says, adding that customers running the private enterprise were not impacted.
In a post-mortem of the incident, the maintainer says that the following LiteLLM artifacts were affected in the attack:
- PyPI: litellm==1.107.0: all seven wheels, live from 11:39:51 to 13:23 UTC
- Docker Hub: v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, and main-stable: pointed to compromised image index sha256:1bbcb1443bc962e45f5aad53fe3d2c30600e0379715fb6c664cdd3ac126c339e from 11:46:56 to 14:20 UTC

articles.title: Cambridge Analytica : Meta condamnée à 25 milliards de dollars pour avoir trompé ses utilisateurs

Huit ans après, le scandale Cambridge Analytica colle encore à la peau de Meta. L’entreprise se voit infliger l’une des amendes les plus lourdes de l’histoire des États-Unis.

articles.title: AI Changes the Data Interface, Not the Query Engine
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- An AI agent that reads Parquet still depends on an execution engine; AI changes the analytical interface and interpretation layer, not the need for precise computation.
- Separate deterministic computation from probabilistic reasoning. Engines should filter, aggregate, and join, while agents should interpret evidence and communicate conclusions.
- An embedded engine such as DuckDB can be sufficient when the data volume is moderate, the primary consumer is the agent workflow, and writes are controlled.
- A managed lakehouse becomes valuable when data has multiple independent consumers, must join with large shared datasets, requires concurrent writes, or needs organization-wide governance.
- Production-grade agent analytics should retain the source data, configuration, derived facts, and model outputs so that every report can be validated and replayed.
AI agents can now generate analytical code, read files from object storage, and turn operational data into structured reports. Does that make data lakes, lakehouses, and SQL engines obsolete? We encountered this question while automating the analysis of a large disaster-recovery exercise. Our first working design stored thirty-second service metrics as Parquet in S3-compatible object storage, used DuckDB for deterministic aggregation, and asked an AI agent to classify failover outcomes and explain the evidence. Pour atteindre une épaisseur de 5,2 mm une fois ouvert, il a fallu amputer l’appareil du module TrueDepth nécessaire au fonctionnement de Face ID. Les utilisateurs devront se contenter de Touch ID dans le bouton latéral du smartphone.
Il est logique de penser qu’Apple cherchera à corriger le tir dans les prochaines versions de l’appareil, mais à partir de laquelle ? Dès l’iPhone Duo 2 ? Selon Mark Gurman, journaliste de Bloomberg, qui s’exprimait ce jeudi 22 octobre, Apple y travaille déjà, avec en prime une nouveauté technique ; rien n’est toutefois arrêté.
Apple testerait un Face ID sous l’écran pour l’iPhone Duo 2
Dans son podcast Power On diffusé ce jeudi 22 octobre, Mark Gurman avance qu’Apple travaille à l’intégration de Face ID sous l’écran de son prochain iPhone pliable. Une innovation que l’on attend également pour l’iPhone qui fêtera les 20 ans de la gamme, attendu l’an prochain.
