articles.title: Node.js Brotli Decoder Bug Could Allow Remote Code Execution in All Supported Versions
articles.summary:
Node.js released security updates on October 21 for its three supported release lines, 22.x, 24.x and 26.x, fixing 10 flaws. The most serious is a bug in the Brotli decompression code that Node.js bundles, which the project says can allow remote code execution, meaning an attacker could run code of their choosing on the affected system.
Each supported line has one fixed version: 22.23.4 and 24.22.1 on the long-term support lines, and 26.12.1 on the current line. Node.js 20.x and earlier have reached end of life and will not receive the fix, so they should be moved to a supported line.
The Brotli flaw is in code Node.js bundles, not in a user's own program. Node.js runs that code whenever it decompresses Brotli data, either directly through the node:zlib module or automatically when code calls fetch() on a response sent with Brotli compression.
An application is exposed where it decompresses Brotli data an attacker controls, such as a request body or a response fetched from another server.
The Brotli Flaw
The flaw is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder, set off by malformed compressed input. The fix is an upstream patch from the Brotli project that Node.js copied in, and it makes the decoder catch invalid input and stop earlier rather than writing past the buffer.
Brotli is Google's compression library, and Node.js ships its own copy. The same fix shipped in Brotli 1.2.1, 1.1.1, and 1.0.10 on October 21, so other software that bundles Brotli may need the same update. …

articles.title: Leaked Trailer Shows the Mass Effect Game BioWare Was Making Before EA Shut It Down
articles.summary:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Leaked Trailer Shows the Mass Effect Game BioWare Was Making Before EA Shut It Down
A day after EA shut down BioWare, a trailer for the canceled next Mass Effect game has leaked online, and it seems the game was going to be called Mass Effect: Universe. Reddit user Random_Hyabusa_Ninja posted the roughly two-minute clip on r/masseffect on October 22, first in the replies of another post, and then as a standalone post. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier has since confirmed on Bluesky that it's a real trailer for the Mass Effect game BioWare was working on up until the closure. The clip is a cinematic rather than gameplay. It follows a new human protagonist, with no sign of Shepard, through a tense bar conversation with an Asari who appears to be Liara T'Soni, cuts to a few gunfights and a Krogan, and ends on the Mass Effect: Universe logo.
The leak also raises questions about how far along the game actually was. EA's internal memo described it as being in early development, and around 50 of the 400 jobs EA is cutting were tied to it. However, a Reddit user claiming to be an EA employee said the trailer had been ready for months and that the project was further along than people think. BioWare first teased the game back in 2020, so that claim doesn't seem far-fetched, but its source is questionable at best. There's no word from EA on the leak so far, though it's reasonable to expect takedown requests to follow.

articles.title: Micron Walks Away From 4F² DRAM After Two Decades of Research, Bets on 3D DRAM Instead
articles.summary:
Thursday, October 22nd 2026
Micron Walks Away From 4F² DRAM After Two Decades of Research, Bets on 3D DRAM Instead
Micron has decided not to bring 4F² DRAM to market, even though it says it invented the cell design and has been researching it for around two decades. Scott DeBoer, Micron's President and Chief Technology and Products Officer, shared the decision during the company's technology webinar on October 21. On paper, 4F² uses vertical channel transistors to shrink each memory cell's footprint by about a third compared with the 6F² layout used in today's DRAM. However, DeBoer argued that real-world density is limited by how closely the capacitors can be packed, not by the cell's footprint, calling the density advantage over 6F² "a bit of a myth." He also said 4F² can be built, but at a higher cost and complexity, and that it runs into fundamental scaling problems at leading-edge nodes, which points toward 3D DRAM instead.
That puts Micron at odds with its rivals. Samsung and SK hynix are both developing 4F² designs, and China's CXMT says its first 4F² product will be a server DDR5 RDIMM due by the end of this year. Micron will keep scaling 6F² instead, with its 1-delta node set to ramp in Boise, Idaho, in the second half of 2027 and the 1-epsilon node after it moving to wafer bonding. 3D DRAM is being developed as a parallel path, but there's no timeline yet, and Micron says it will only switch once the economics make sense. articles.title: OpenCode Flaw Lets Malicious MCP Servers Execute Code During Sign-In on Windows and WSL
articles.summary:
A flaw in the OpenCode AI coding agent allowed a malicious or hijacked MCP server to run code on a developer's Windows or WSL machine when the developer signed in. OpenCode connects to MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers to add outside tools, and such code would run with the developer's own access.
Anomaly, the company behind OpenCode, fixed the flaw in version 1.18.33 on September 28. It did not request a CVE or publish a security advisory, so vulnerability scanners will not flag the builds still at risk: 1.0.137 through 1.18.32.
During that sign-in, the server itself supplies the web address the user is sent to, an OAuth "authorization endpoint." On Windows and WSL, OpenCode handed that address to a helper that opens it in a browser. The helper built a PowerShell command around the address without escaping it, so an address written to carry a PowerShell command would run that command.
The browser step runs only when a developer starts the sign-in, by running opencode mcp auth or making the matching request. Having the server configured, or opening a session, does not reach it.
The attacker needs control of a remote MCP server the developer has added, and that server need not be hostile from the start. One that is later taken over, or a domain that changes hands, could carry the same address.
Pillar Security, which found the flaw and disclosed it on October 19, rates it critical, with a proposed severity score of 9.8 out of 10.

articles.title: Railway Says Intruder May Have Accessed Customer Secrets, Urges Credential Rotation
articles.summary:
Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) provider Railway on Wednesday disclosed "anomalous activity" related to systems that store customer environment variables.
Upon further investigation, the company found that an unauthorized third party may have gained access to encrypted environment variables, and, in some cases, obtained the decrypted contents. The impact, it said, is limited to a "subset of users," although it did not disclose an exact number.
Environment variables refer to user-defined key-value pairs that are used to store sensitive data like API keys, database credentials, or feature flags. They are configured at the operating system or container environment level instead of hard-coding the values directly into a program's source code.
Railway said the incident is likely part of a series of attacks designed to target platform companies with the ultimate goal of compromising artificial intelligence (AI) inference providers. The company also said it has notified upstream providers to proactively revoke the keys so as to prevent their abuse.
Customers are being urged to take the following actions as a precautionary measure -
- Rotate environment variables, including any API keys, stored in Railway, as well as private registry credentials.
- Review logs for those services for unusual activity

articles.title: Cómo funciona PHP, qué es y por qué un fallo en su sistema pone en riesgo la seguridad de miles de páginas web
articles.summary:
Una serie de vulnerabilidades críticas en PHP, uno de los lenguajes de programación más utilizados para desarrollar sitios web y aplicaciones, encendió las alertas internacionales de ciberseguridad después de que investigadores identificaran fallos que habrían permanecido ocultos durante años.
El hallazgo, realizado con ayuda de herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA), llevó a gobiernos y organizaciones a recomendar actualizaciones urgentes e incluso la desconexión temporal de algunas plataformas.
Entre los servicios que adoptaron medidas preventivas figuran sitios de Wikimedia, la organización responsable de Wikipedia, además de páginas de organismos públicos de Europa.
En Reino Unido, las autoridades informaron que 32 servicios gubernamentales estaban fuera de servicio en medio de la alerta global, aunque atribuyeron buena parte de las interrupciones a decisiones preventivas y no confirmaron que todos los casos estuvieran directamente relacionados con la explotación de estas vulnerabilidades.
Las empresas de ciberseguridad Wiz y Calif participaron en la investigación de los fallos, mientras que OpenAI confirmó que su tecnología de inteligencia artificial contribuyó a identificar problemas en el código. articles.title: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD RCE Flaws Disclosed on Public Mailing Lists Before Kernel Fixes
articles.summary:
Linux servers running KSMBD, the kernel's built-in SMB server, are exposed to two publicly reported remote code execution flaws rated 9.0 by Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative, with no fix yet in the mainline kernel.
One of them, ZDI-CAN-33774, can be triggered before any network authentication. The other, ZDI-CAN-33549, requires the SMB Direct transport and an RDMA-capable network interface.
ZDI-CAN-33549 is an integer underflow in KSMBD's SMB Direct path. A client can supply RDMA buffer descriptors in which the first is longer than the declared payload, causing the server's size counter to wrap and allowing a subsequent memory copy to overrun the end of an allocated buffer.
It requires three things: an RDMA-capable interface (hardware or the rxe software driver), a writable KSMBD share, and a client negotiating SMB Direct.
ZDI-CAN-33774 requires no authentication, exposing any server running KSMBD on port 445. The flaw is a race in how KSMBD assigns its handler table: a burst of short SMB1 packets followed by an SMB2 packet in the same TCP write causes workers to handle SMB1 data with an SMB2 handler, reading past the end of the shorter buffer. A path to writing past the buffer also exists once an attacker has access to a share.

Six of those eight were for website (TLS) certificates. Chrome will stop trusting the eMudhra root certificate above them, emSign ECC Root CA - G3. The change is expected to reach users on the morning of October 27, Pacific time.
On October 20, Mozilla decided to stop trusting the same root in Firefox. Removing a root from a browser also cuts off legitimate certificates issued beneath it.
About 30,800 unexpired certificates chained to that root as of October 21, by Chrome's count of public Certificate Transparency (CT) logs. Of those, 99.9% were issued through InCommon, the certificate service Internet2 created for the higher education community. InCommon moved the service onto eMudhra's CertiNext platform between April and July this year.
Google has told website operators with certificates under that root that they "must immediately acquire and install a new TLS certificate from another PKI hierarchy included in the Chrome Root Store."

Free l'a annoncée dans un billet des plus succincts, sans nommer la moindre faille ni en préciser la gravité. Une sortie toute en sobriété, qui s'ajoute aux dernières semaines bien chargées pour les box de l'opérateur de Xavier Niel, largement consacrées au Wi-Fi.
Nouvelle mise à jour des Freebox, Free corrige des failles de sécurité sans en dire plus
La mise à jour concerne les Freebox Revolution, Pop, Delta et Ultra. La liste de corrections tient en deux mots, « correctifs de sécurité ». Free n'en dit pas plus. Sur l'application de l'opérateur, on évoque un « renforcement de la sécurité et de la protection du système ». C'est une prudence qu'on peut comprendre, puisque détailler une faille avant que toutes les box soient corrigées pourrait tendre la perche aux cybercriminels.
Pour l'installer, Free demande simplement de redémarrer le Freebox Server. L'application Free permet de le faire en quelques secondes. Freebox OS aussi, via le menu « Free » en bas à gauche, tout comme les flèches de la box elle-même. articles.title: C’est officiel, Arc Browser a une date de fin et elle approche
articles.summary:
The Browser Company coupera Arc le 22 décembre sur Mac et Windows, puis effacera sous trente jours les données personnelles liées aux comptes. Ses fidèles ont donc deux mois pour passer sur Dia, le navigateur à IA conçu par l’équipe d’Arc, ou sauvegarder leurs onglets ailleurs.
Tout a une fin, sauf la banane, qui en a deux. Les utilisateurs d’Arc savaient la fin proche, puisque leur navigateur ne gagnait plus aucune fonction depuis mai 2025. Ils connaissent maintenant la date. Dans son message d’adieu, relayé sur son compte X, The Browser Company met en avant la sécurité. « Maintenir un navigateur sécurisé demande un travail constant et dédié qui ne fait que s’intensifier à l’ère de l’IA », écrit l’éditeur new-yorkais, qui préfère consacrer ses ingénieurs à Dia, désormais disponible sur Windows en plus du Mac. L’arrêt se fera en trois étapes, et vos données seront effacées après la dernière si vous ne les avez pas sauvegardées.
Arc Search privé d’IA en novembre, comptes désactivés en décembre
Plus personne ne peut créer de compte Arc depuis le 22 octobre. Si vous avez un compte, rien ne change encore, et The Browser Company a ajouté à la dernière version du navigateur une option d’export complet. Grâce à elle, vous pouvez enregistrer vos Spaces et vos onglets sous forme de liste de liens, depuis les réglages avancés d’Arc, jusqu’au 22 décembre.

articles.title: Russia's upgraded Tu-160M bomber promises easier future upgrades
articles.summary:
Russia's B-1 bomber clone set to get new avionics and a 'modular' architecture — new kit can be added later to boost longevity, not unlike the B-52 Stratofortress
Russia is giving its Cold War Tu-160 bomber a digital overhaul
- Russia claims 80% of its Tu-160M bomber systems are modernized
- Russia's Tu-160M retains its Soviet appearance despite extensive internal modernization
- Modular avionics could allow Russia to upgrade bomber electronics individually
Russia is preparing its Tu-160M strategic bomber for future equipment upgrades through a modular avionics system designed to accommodate technological changes throughout its operational life.
The aircraft retains the distinctive appearance of its Soviet predecessor, although Russian aircraft manufacturer Tupolev claims approximately 80% of its onboard equipment has undergone modernization.
This approach could extend the bomber's service life through successive technological upgrades, similar to the modernization strategy employed on America's B-52 Stratofortress.
Modular avionics designed for future upgrades
Tupolev General Director Yuri Abrosimov said the Tu-160M incorporates a redesigned electronics architecture that allows individual components to be replaced as technology advances.
The arrangement is intended to simplify future modernization by allowing engineers to introduce better equipment without rebuilding the aircraft's entire electronic infrastructure.
